description: Weekly payroll for about 78,000 associates (about $65 million a run): pay calculation, tax withholding, garnishments, ACH files to two banks, paycard funding, and checks
process_owner: Senior Vice President, Payroll and Associate Services
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Payroll window runs Monday 06:00 to Thursday 12:00 (Eastern) for Friday pay dates; ACH files must reach the banks by Thursday 14:00; state wage payment timing laws in 38 states; many associates live paycheck to paycheck. Outside the window the MTD is 72 h
source_evidence: EV-070 (Senior Vice President, Payroll and Associate Services interview); EV-054 (weekly payroll value); EV-065 (pay delivery and banks); EV-023 (DR test)
manual_workaround: Repeat the prior week's net pay for associates on continuing assignments as an advance, with true-up the next week; instant paycard funding for hardship cases; courier checks
dependent_systems: SYS-03 payroll engine; SYS-04 time capture; SYS-05 identity platform; integration platform (Cloud A)
dependent_third_parties: Originating banks A and B; paycard program manager; payroll tax filing service; print and mail vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: Payroll operations (about 420 staff in 3 payroll centers); Treasurer
quantified_impact_basis: Off-cycle advances, instant paycard funding fees, overtime, bank fees, and estimated state late-payment penalties and client credits; about $2.4 million per day of delay, not counting reputational harm with associates
acquired_firm_dependency: ACQ-1 clinicians are paid by the ACQ-1 outsourced payroll provider (see BP-16)
single_points_of_failure: Single payroll engine instance (warm standby in second region)

description: Associate clock-in in the mobile app and on 140 on-site time clocks, client approval in the timesheet portal, and time feeds from about 400 client VMS instances (about 46,000 timesheets on a peak day)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Approved time must reach the payroll engine by Monday 12:00 for that week's payroll; time clocks buffer 72 hours of punches offline; client VMS feeds can be re-sent
source_evidence: EV-070 (Chief Operating Officer interview); EV-055 (timesheet volume); EV-013 (time clock buffer and server)
manual_workaround: Branches collect paper or spreadsheet timesheets signed by client supervisors; time clock punches exported from the clock buffer; client VMS reports uploaded manually
dependent_systems: SYS-04 time capture app and portal; time clock server (DC-1); integration platform; SYS-05
dependent_third_parties: Time capture vendor; client VMS providers; time clock vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: Branch staff; on-site supervisors; client approvers
quantified_impact_basis: Manual reconstruction and re-keying of about 46,000 timesheets, pay errors, and client disputes
single_points_of_failure: Time clock server in DC-1 (single instance, unsupported OS)

description: Weekly invoices (about $92 million a week), VMS invoice submission for managed-program clients, cash application
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Cash: about $18.5 million is invoiced per business day; clients pay on terms, so a few days of delay defers cash rather than losing it; VMS invoice cut-offs are weekly
source_evidence: EV-070 (Chief Financial Officer interview); EV-054 (invoices per business day)
manual_workaround: Hold invoices; prioritize the top 50 clients from payroll engine reports; submit VMS invoices manually
quantified_impact_basis: Invoices delayed about $18.5 million per business day; borrowing cost about $70,000 per day of delay (fictional revolving credit rate)

business_process: Candidate sourcing, recruiting, and job order fulfillment
description: Career sites, applications (about 2.6 million a year), AI ranking (AI-001), recruiter search and submittals, job orders from about 9,500 clients
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About 960 new associates start each business day; unfilled orders move to competitors within a day; client fill-rate commitments in managed programs
source_evidence: EV-070 (Vice President, Talent Acquisition Technology interview); EV-055 (applications and daily starts)
manual_workaround: Recruiters work from exported hot lists and phone; job boards collect applications directly; priority orders filled from redeployable associates
dependent_systems: SYS-01 ATS and CRM; AI ranking add-on; SYS-05
dependent_third_parties: ATS vendor; AI ranking vendor; job boards
quantified_impact_basis: About 30% of new starts slip by a day: lost and delayed gross profit, plus recruiter idle time
acquired_firm_dependency: ACQ-1 uses its own legacy ATS (BP-16)

business_process: Associate onboarding, Form I-9, and E-Verify
description: Tax and direct deposit forms, electronic Form I-9 with document examination, E-Verify cases for about 960 new hires a business day
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Form I-9 Section 2 within 3 business days of hire (8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(ii)); E-Verify case within 3 business days (MOU Art. II.A.9); if E-Verify is down, document the outage (Florida example: Fla. Stat. 448.095(2)(c))
source_evidence: EV-070 (Vice President, Employment Compliance interview); EV-055 (new hires); EV-035 (Form I-9 and E-Verify procedures)
manual_workaround: Paper Form I-9 at branches with later entry; E-Verify cases created after recovery with the outage documented; associates start work only after Section 1 is complete
dependent_systems: SYS-02 onboarding and I-9 platform; E-Verify; SYS-05
dependent_people_or_facilities: Onboarding and compliance specialists (about 650); branch staff
quantified_impact_basis: About 960 starts a business day delayed or completed on paper; rework; exposure for late Forms I-9
acquired_firm_dependency: ACQ-1 completes Forms I-9 in its legacy system (BP-16)

description: FCRA disclosures and authorizations, report ordering through two screening providers, adjudication, pre-adverse and adverse action notices (about 190,000 checks a year)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Most commercial and healthcare clients require a cleared check before the start date; FCRA notice sequence must be preserved (15 U.S.C. 1681b(b)(3))
source_evidence: EV-070 (Vice President, Employment Compliance interview); EV-038 (provider split); EV-072 (volume shift exercise)
manual_workaround: Order directly in the screening providers' portals; shift volume to the second provider
dependent_third_parties: Screening providers 1 and 2; drug testing provider

business_process: Healthcare clinician credentialing and compliance files
description: License, certification, immunization, and competency files that must be current before a clinician works a shift at a hospital
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Patient safety at client hospitals: a clinician with a lapsed license must not work; hospital contracts require current files before each shift
source_evidence: EV-070 (President, Healthcare Staffing interview); EV-057 (ACQ-1 status); EV-058 (ACQ-1 credentialing system)
manual_workaround: Primary-source license checks on state board sites; hospital credentialing offices confirm by phone; hold new starts
dependent_systems: SYS-01 credentialing module; ACQ-1 credentialing system; SYS-05
dependent_third_parties: Credential verification service; ACQ-1 legacy system vendor
quantified_impact_basis: About 9,000 clinicians a week; cancelled shifts and hospital penalties; safety impact dominates
acquired_firm_dependency: Yes: 6,500 ACQ-1 clinicians are credentialed in the ACQ-1 legacy system
single_points_of_failure: ACQ-1 credentialing system (single instance, vendor-hosted, no tested restore)

business_process: SL-1 Workforce Management Platform (managed service provider programs)

description: Client-sourced workers (about 6,000 a week for about 340 clients) are hired, onboarded, and paid through the firm's payroll
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Same payroll window as BP-01; client contracts commit to on-time pay and accurate client reports; processing integrity commitments (P09)

description: Contact center for associates: pay questions, bank and address changes, W-2 reprints, about 21,000 calls and chats a day

source_evidence: EV-071 (Vice President, Associate Service Center interview); EV-043 (call volume)

business_process: Payroll tax filing, garnishments, and year-end forms
description: Federal, state, and local tax deposits and returns, garnishment remittances, and about 310,000 W-2s each January
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Deposit and filing deadlines; year-end W-2 window in January shortens MTD to 48 h
source_evidence: EV-071 (Controller interview); EV-066 (tax filing records); EV-054 (W-2 count)

description: Biweekly payroll for 12,000 internal employees (about $38 million a run), HR records, benefits enrollment
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Payroll cutoff 72 hours before pay date; SOX-relevant
source_evidence: EV-071 (Chief Human Resources Officer interview); EV-054 (internal staff payroll)
manual_workaround: Repeat prior payroll with adjustments through the HCM provider
quantified_impact_basis: Manual adjustments and penalties if payroll is late

description: Quarterly and annual close, SOX controls, 10-Q and 10-K preparation

source_evidence: EV-070 (Chief Financial Officer interview); EV-071 (Controller interview)
manual_workaround: Extend the close calendar; manual journal entry controls with dual approval
dependent_systems: SYS-10 ERP; SYS-03 (revenue and payroll subledgers); data platform (Cloud B)
quantified_impact_basis: Overtime and audit fees; a late filing would be Severe

description: Staffing for 34 federal contracts and 21 state agency contracts: agency timekeeping, invoicing, and contract reporting; federal contract information (FCI) in SYS-01 and SYS-03
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Agency invoicing cycles and contract reporting deadlines; FAR 52.204-21 safeguarding for FCI; agency incident reporting under contract terms
source_evidence: EV-071 (Vice President, Government Solutions interview); EV-047 (federal and state agency contracts)

description: About 380 branches and 140 on-site offices: walk-in applicants, lobby kiosks, local printing, badge issuance, and associate dispatch

source_evidence: EV-070 (Chief Operating Officer interview); EV-056 (sites); EV-014 (SD-WAN and failover)
